title: Development and Content Validation of a Spanish-Language Drug-Drug Interaction Causality Assessment Scale
content: Drug–drug interactions may result in adverse clinical events; however, identifying a potential interaction does not necessarily establish causality in an individual patient. This study aimed to develop a Spanish-language scale for the structured assessment of suspected drug–drug interaction causality and to obtain evidence of its content validity. The initial version was developed from literature and previous causality assessment scale. Its content was evaluated through three rounds of a modified Delphi process involving 17 experts. The resulting version was subsequently applied to 10 clinical cases during pilot testing, and the modifications arising from this stage were evaluated through a second modified Delphi process involving 11 independent experts. The initial version comprised nine items across five domains. Following both Delphi processes and pilot testing, a final version comprising nine items organized into four domains was obtained. In the final round, the overall Aiken’s V values were 0.97 for relevance, 0.95 for coherence, and 0.94 for clarity and comprehensibility, and 0.94 for sufficiency. The scale showed favorable evidence of content validity; however, its inter-rater reliability and criterion validity remain to be evaluated.
